name: HIGH CARD POOL
description: High Card Pool, often called Red Dog or Slippery Sam, is a fast-paced banking game where players bet on whether a card dealt after their initial hand will match a suit in their hand and have a higher rank. It is a game of probability and betting psychology, common in both casual social settings and older casino environments.

content.text: High Card Pool, often called Red Dog or Slippery Sam, is a fast-paced banking game where players bet on whether a card dealt after their initial hand will match a suit in their hand and have a higher rank. It is a game of probability and betting psychology, common in both casual social settings and older casino environments.

Originating in the 19th century, it was frequently played in American mining camps and on riverboats. The name 'Red Dog' originally referred to this specific pool-based betting game before being co-opted by the 'In-Between' casino game.
The dealer deals 5 cards face down to each player (4 or 3 cards in some variants to accommodate more players).

items.text: Four cards: Only four cards are dealt to each player to allow a larger number of players without running out of cards.
Three cards: Only three cards are dealt to each player to accommodate more players.
Dealer bank: Red Dog can be played with a bank put up by the dealer (as in Shoot or Slippery Sam); players do not ante, and if the pot becomes empty the deal immediately passes to the next player.
